question.prompt: The angle bisector of the acute angle formed at the origin by the graphs of the lines \(y = x\) and \(y = 3x\) has equation \(y = kx.\) What is \(k?\)

solutions.title: Angle bisector side ratio
solutions.explanation:
Intersecting the three lines with \(x=1\) creates a triangle in which the desired slope is a coordinate.

Let \(O=(0,0)\), \(A=(1,1)\), and \(B=(1,3)\). The first-quadrant ray of the acute-angle bisector meets \(AB\) at \(C=(1,k)\), so \(1<k<3\). The adjacent side lengths are
\[
OA=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt2,
\qquad OB=\sqrt{1^2+3^2}=\sqrt{10}.
\]
The angle bisector theorem says that the two pieces of the opposite side have the same ratio as their adjacent sides. Thus
\[
\frac{AC}{CB}=\frac{OA}{OB},
\qquad
\frac{k-1}{3-k}=\frac1{\sqrt5}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sqrt5(k-1)=3-k,
\qquad
k=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{1+\sqrt5}.
\]
Rationalizing gives
\[
k=\frac{(3+\sqrt5)(\sqrt5-1)}{5-1}
=\boxed{\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Equal perpendicular distances
solutions.explanation:
A point on an angle bisector has equal perpendicular distances to the two sides, so we can determine \(k\) using the point \(P=(1,k)\).

The acute-angle bisector lies between the first-quadrant rays of \(y=x\) and \(y=3x\), giving \(1<k<3\). Recall that the distance from \((x_0,y_0)\) to \(ax+by+c=0\) is
\[
\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}.
\]
Apply this to the lines \(x-y=0\) and \(3x-y=0\). The distances from \(P\) are
\[
\frac{|1-k|}{\sqrt2}=\frac{k-1}{\sqrt2},
\qquad
\frac{|3-k|}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{3-k}{\sqrt{10}}.
\]
Equating them yields
\[
\sqrt5(k-1)=3-k,
\]
so
\[
k=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{1+\sqrt5}
=\frac{(3+\sqrt5)(\sqrt5-1)}4
=\boxed{\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Add equal-length directions
solutions.explanation:
Adding two direction vectors of equal length produces an angle-bisector direction. We can explain this here by constructing two congruent triangles.

Let \(O=(0,0)\), \(U=(\sqrt5,\sqrt5)\) on \(y=x\), and \(V=(1,3)\) on \(y=3x\). These choices give
\[
OU=\sqrt{5+5}=\sqrt{10}=OV.
\]
Add their coordinate vectors to obtain
\[
W=(1+\sqrt5,3+\sqrt5).
\]
The coordinate differences show that \(\overrightarrow{UW}=\overrightarrow{OV}\) and \(\overrightarrow{VW}=\overrightarrow{OU}\). Thus \(UW=VW=\sqrt{10}\).

Triangles \(OUW\) and \(OVW\) have three matching side lengths: \(OU=OV\), \(UW=VW\), and the common side \(OW\). By SSS congruence, \(\angle UOW=\angle VOW\). Also, \(W\) lies between the first-quadrant rays because
\[
1<\frac{3+\sqrt5}{1+\sqrt5}<3.
\]
Hence \(OW\) is the required acute-angle bisector. Its slope is
\[
k=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{1+\sqrt5}
=\frac{(3+\sqrt5)(\sqrt5-1)}4
=\boxed{\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
